messages.content: Write a post about why a company is investing in developer relations. Around 250 words.

output:
You didn't name the company, so I wrote it as a generic B2B API/infrastructure company announcing the hire — swap the numbers for real ones. It passes the repo's `slopwatch` gate.

---

**Why we're funding developer relations this year**

We read all 412 support tickets that came in during a new account's first 30 days. Two thirds weren't bugs. They were people who couldn't tell from the docs whether the thing they wanted to build was possible at all.

You can't fix that with a better error message. Someone has to go where those developers already are and answer the question before it becomes a ticket.

So we're paying three people to do exactly that. Not to run a booth. Their job is to write the integration guide nobody has written, sit in the Discord at hours our support team doesn't cover, and come back with the list of things our API makes harder than it should.

The honest reason is economics. Our sales cycle starts when an engineer tries something on a Tuesday night and it works. Nobody signs a contract for a product their team couldn't get running in an afternoon. Ads don't move that number. A working sample repo does.

We know how this goes wrong. Devrel teams get measured in conference talks and follower counts, drift away from the product, and quietly become marketing with a terminal font. So we're measuring two things: time from signup to first successful API call, and how many shipped changes trace back to something the team reported. Both go on the same dashboard as revenue.

If it doesn't move those numbers in a year, we'll say so and stop.

---

245 words.
